title: MultiNorm: Spatially Aware Normalisation of Multi-Slice Spatial Transcriptomics Data
text: MultiNorm spatially aware normalisation method developed multi-slice spatial transcriptomics data. method accounts unwanted variation within tissue slices aiming preserve biologically meaningful spatial expression patterns signals. vignette, demonstrate application MultiNorm using four human dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) tissue slices available spatialLIBD package.

title: MultiNorm: Spatially Aware Normalisation of Multi-Slice Spatial Transcriptomics Data
text: MultiNorm accepts named list SpatialExperiment objects, object represents individual tissue slice. demonstration, select four tissue slices DLPFC dataset split combined SpatialExperiment object individual objects.
code: # Select four tissue slices sample_ids = 151507:151510  # Split the combined SpatialExperiment object into individual slices spe_list <- setNames(   lapply(sample_ids, function(id) {     spe[, spe$sample_id == id]   }),   sample_ids )  # Inspect the dimensions of each tissue slice lapply(spe_list, dim) #> $`151507` #> [1] 33538  4226 #>  #> $`151508` #> [1] 33538  4384 #>  #> $`151509` #> [1] 33538  4789 #>  #> $`151510` #> [1] 33538  4634

title: MultiNorm: Spatially Aware Normalisation of Multi-Slice Spatial Transcriptomics Data
text: Although comprehensive quality control procedures can applied depending characteristics dataset, perform minimal quality control demonstration purposes. Specifically, remove spots zero total counts genes expressed selected tissue slices.
code: # Remove spots with zero total counts independently from each slice spe_list_qc <- lapply(spe_list, function(spe) {   spe[, colSums(counts(spe)) > 0] })  # Combine count matrices across all tissue slices combined_counts <- do.call(cbind, lapply(spe_list_qc, counts))  # Identify genes expressed in at least one spot across all slices keep_genes <- rowSums(combined_counts) > 0  # Retain the same set of expressed genes in all slices spe_list_qc <- lapply(spe_list_qc, function(spe) {   spe[keep_genes, ] })  # Inspect the dimensions before and after quality control lapply(spe_list, dim) #> $`151507` #> [1] 33538  4226 #>  #> $`151508` #> [1] 33538  4384 #>  #> $`151509` #> [1] 33538  4789 #>  #> $`151510` #> [1] 33538  4634 lapply(spe_list_qc, dim) #> $`151507` #> [1] 23493  4226 #>  #> $`151508` #> [1] 23493  4384 #>  #> $`151509` #> [1] 23493  4789 #>  #> $`151510` #> [1] 23493  4634

title: MultiNorm: Spatially Aware Normalisation of Multi-Slice Spatial Transcriptomics Data
text: reduce computational requirements demonstration, restrict analysis subset highly variable genes (HVGs). top 2,000 HVGs identified independently tissue slice using scran package. subsequently retain intersection gene sets ensure tissue slices contain common set highly variable genes. Log-normalisation performed temporarily HVG selection. original raw counts retained subsequent application MultiNorm. Note HVG selection performed reduce computational requirements demonstration. Users may choose different set genes depending analytical objectives.
code: library(scran) #> Loading required package: scuttle library(scuttle) library(SpatialExperiment)  # Identify the top 2,000 HVGs independently for each slice hvg_list <- lapply(spe_list_qc, function(spe) {    # Temporarily log-normalise counts for HVG selection   spe <- scuttle::logNormCounts(spe)    # Model gene-level expression variance   dec <- scran::modelGeneVar(spe)    # Select the top 2,000 highly variable genes   scran::getTopHVGs(dec, n = 2000) })  # Identify HVGs shared across all tissue slices common_hvgs <- Reduce(intersect, hvg_list)  # Examine the number of shared HVGs length(common_hvgs) #> [1] 890  # Retain the common HVGs in each tissue slice spe_list_hvg <- lapply(spe_list_qc, function(spe) {   spe[common_hvgs, ] })  # Inspect the dimensions after HVG selection lapply(spe_list_hvg, dim) #> $`151507` #> [1]  890 4226 #>  #> $`151508` #> [1]  890 4384 #>  #> $`151509` #> [1]  890 4789 #>  #> $`151510` #> [1]  890 4634

title: MultiNorm: Spatially Aware Normalisation of Multi-Slice Spatial Transcriptomics Data
text: MultiNorm utilises information biologically similar regions across tissue slices help distinguish unwanted variation genuine biological differences. regions can identified using existing spatial clustering integration methods, spatialMNN, BANKSY appropriate cross-slice cluster matching, suitable methods. Alternatively, users may provide existing biological annotations, cell-type labels manually annotated anatomical regions, available. demonstration, use spatialMNN method identify biologically similar regions, referred niches, across four DLPFC slices.

title: MultiNorm: Spatially Aware Normalisation of Multi-Slice Spatial Transcriptomics Data
text: following helper function converts SpatialExperiment objects Seurat objects, identifies spatial clusters within individual tissue slices, matches biologically similar clusters across slices, transfers resulting niche annotations back original SpatialExperiment objects. apply function identify biologically similar niches across four tissue slices. Spots without assigned niche annotations removed applying MultiNorm.
code: library(SpatialExperiment) library(atlasClustering) #> Warning: replacing previous import 'dplyr::as_data_frame' by #> 'igraph::as_data_frame' when loading 'atlasClustering' #> Warning: replacing previous import 'Seurat::components' by 'igraph::components' #> when loading 'atlasClustering' #> Warning: replacing previous import 'dplyr::groups' by 'igraph::groups' when #> loading 'atlasClustering' #> Warning: replacing previous import 'DescTools::%c%' by 'igraph::%c%' when #> loading 'atlasClustering' #> Warning: replacing previous import 'dplyr::union' by 'igraph::union' when #> loading 'atlasClustering' #> Warning: replacing previous import 'circlize::degree' by 'igraph::degree' when #> loading 'atlasClustering' #> Warning: replacing previous import 'igraph::normalize' by 'scater::normalize' #> when loading 'atlasClustering' library(stringr) library(Seurat) #> Loading required package: SeuratObject #> Loading required package: sp #>  #> Attaching package: 'sp' #> The following object is masked from 'package:IRanges': #>  #>     %over% #>  #> Attaching package: 'SeuratObject' #> The following object is masked from 'package:SummarizedExperiment': #>  #>     Assays #> The following object is masked from 'package:GenomicRanges': #>  #>     intersect #> The following object is masked from 'package:Seqinfo': #>  #>     intersect #> The following object is masked from 'package:IRanges': #>  #>     intersect #> The following object is masked from 'package:S4Vectors': #>  #>     intersect #> The following object is masked from 'package:BiocGenerics': #>  #>     intersect #> The following objects are masked from 'package:base': #>  #>     intersect, t #>  #> Attaching package: 'Seurat' #> The following object is masked from 'package:SummarizedExperiment': #>  #>     Assays  run_niche_mnn <- function(spe_list,r1=1,r2=0.5) {    # Clean spot-level metadata and remove duplicated gene identifiers    spe_list <- lapply(spe_list, function(x) {     cd <- colData(x)      if ("X" %in% colnames(cd)) {       colnames(cd)[colnames(cd) == "X"] <- "index"       colData(x) <- cd     }      x <- x[!duplicated(rownames(x)), ]     return(x)   })    # Assign a unique sample identifier to each tissue slice    for (i in seq_along(spe_list)) {     colData(spe_list[[i]])$sample_id <- names(spe_list)[i]   }    # Define a helper function to convert SpatialExperiment objects   # into Seurat objects while retaining spatial coordinates and   # relevant spot-level metadata    spe2seu_single <- function(spe_obj, sample_name = NULL,                             sel_assay = "counts", sel_col = "LS") {      if (is.null(sample_name)) sample_name <- spe_obj$sample[1]      meta_df <- data.frame(       barcode = colnames(spe_obj),       coord_x = int_colData(spe_obj)$spatialCoords[, 1],       coord_y = int_colData(spe_obj)$spatialCoords[, 2],       row.names = colnames(assays(spe_obj)[[sel_assay]])     )      if (!is.null(sel_col)) {       for (col in sel_col) {         meta_df[[col]] <- colData(spe_obj)[[col]]       }     }      seu <- CreateSeuratObject(       counts = assays(spe_obj)[[sel_assay]],       project = paste0("spe_", sample_name),       meta.data = meta_df     )      seu <- FindVariableFeatures(seu, verbose = FALSE)     return(seu)   }    niche_spe <- spe_list    # Convert each SpatialExperiment object into a Seurat object    seurat_ls <- mapply(     spe2seu_single,     niche_spe,     names(niche_spe),     SIMPLIFY = FALSE   )    # Stage 1: Identify spatial clusters within individual tissue slices    seurat_ls <- stage_1(     seurat_ls,     find_HVG = FALSE,     top_pcs = 8,     cor_threshold = 0.6,     cor_met = "PC",     edge_smoothing = TRUE,     nn = 6,     use_glmpca = TRUE,     verbose = TRUE,     cl_resolution = r1   )    # Stage 2: Match biologically similar clusters across tissue slices   # using the MNN-based approach    rtn_ls <- stage_2(     seurat_ls,     cl_key = "merged_cluster",     rtn_seurat = TRUE,     nn_2 = 10,     method = "MNN",     top_pcs = 8,     use_glmpca = TRUE,     rare_ct = "m",     resolution = r2,     hvg = nrow(spe_list[[1]])   )    # Assign shared MNN-based cluster labels to the Seurat objects    seurat_ls <- assign_label(     seurat_ls,     rtn_ls$cl_df,     "MNN",     0.6,     cl_key = "merged_cluster"   )    # Transfer the shared niche annotations back to the original   # SpatialExperiment objects using spot barcodes    for (sample_name in names(seurat_ls)) {      seu <- seurat_ls[[sample_name]]     clusters <- seu@meta.data$sec_cluster_MNN     barcodes <- colnames(seu)      spe_obj <- spe_list[[sample_name]]      colData(spe_obj)$sec_cluster_MNN <- NA     colData(spe_obj)[barcodes, "niche"] <- clusters      spe_list[[sample_name]] <- spe_obj   }    return(spe_list)  } spe_list_hvg = run_niche_mnn(spe_list_hvg) #> spe_151507 cluster number: 172 #> Warning: Using `size` aesthetic for lines was deprecated in ggplot2 3.4.0. #> ℹ Please use `linewidth` instead. #> ℹ The deprecated feature was likely used in the atlasClustering package. #>   Please report the issue to the authors. #> This warning is displayed once per session. #> Call `lifecycle::last_lifecycle_warnings()` to see where this warning was #> generated. #> Warning: `aes_string()` was deprecated in ggplot2 3.0.0. #> ℹ Please use tidy evaluation idioms with `aes()`. #> ℹ See also `vignette("ggplot2-in-packages")` for more information. #> ℹ The deprecated feature was likely used in the atlasClustering package. #>   Please report the issue to the authors. #> This warning is displayed once per session. #> Call `lifecycle::last_lifecycle_warnings()` to see where this warning was #> generated. #> spe_151507 merged cluster number: 37 #> spe_151508 cluster number: 121 #> spe_151508 merged cluster number: 33 #> spe_151509 cluster number: 72 #> spe_151509 merged cluster number: 30 #> spe_151510 cluster number: 99 #> spe_151510 merged cluster number: 38 #> Elasped Time: #> 11.3 secs #> Warning: Data is of class matrix. Coercing to dgCMatrix. #> Normalizing layer: counts remove_na_niche <- function(x) {   lapply(x, function(s) {     s[, !is.na(s$niche)]   }) }  spe_list_hvg = remove_na_niche(spe_list_hvg)

text: examine effect MultiNorm unwanted variation, compare distribution log library sizes normalisation across four tissue slices. resulting data frame converted long format facilitate comparison raw normalised library size distributions.
code: library(dplyr) #>  #> Attaching package: 'dplyr' #> The following object is masked from 'package:Biobase': #>  #>     combine #> The following objects are masked from 'package:GenomicRanges': #>  #>     intersect, setdiff, union #> The following object is masked from 'package:Seqinfo': #>  #>     intersect #> The following objects are masked from 'package:IRanges': #>  #>     collapse, desc, intersect, setdiff, slice, union #> The following objects are masked from 'package:S4Vectors': #>  #>     first, intersect, rename, setdiff, setequal, union #> The following objects are masked from 'package:BiocGenerics': #>  #>     combine, intersect, setdiff, setequal, union #> The following object is masked from 'package:generics': #>  #>     explain #> The following object is masked from 'package:matrixStats': #>  #>     count #> The following objects are masked from 'package:stats': #>  #>     filter, lag #> The following objects are masked from 'package:base': #>  #>     intersect, setdiff, setequal, union library(ggplot2) library(Matrix) #>  #> Attaching package: 'Matrix' #> The following object is masked from 'package:S4Vectors': #>  #>     expand  datalogLS <- lapply(names(dlpfc_norm), function(nm) {    spe <- dlpfc_norm[[nm]]    # Calculate log library sizes from raw counts   logLS_raw <- log1p(colSums(counts(spe)))    # Calculate log library sizes from normalised expression values   logLS_norm <- log1p(colSums(expm1(logcounts(spe))))    # Combine raw and normalised library sizes with sample identifiers   data.frame(     method = nm,     sample_id = spe$sample_id,     logLS_raw = logLS_raw,     logLS_norm = logLS_norm   ) }) %>%   bind_rows() library(tidyr) #>  #> Attaching package: 'tidyr' #> The following objects are masked from 'package:Matrix': #>  #>     expand, pack, unpack #> The following object is masked from 'package:S4Vectors': #>  #>     expand  datalogLS_long <- datalogLS %>%   pivot_longer(     cols = c(logLS_raw, logLS_norm),     names_to = "type",     values_to = "logLS"   )

title: Spatially Aware Normalisation for Multi-Slice Spatial Transcriptomics Data
text: MultiNorm R package spatially aware normalisation multi-slice spatial transcriptomics (ST) data. MultiNorm decomposes observed gene expression variation biological technical components. method aims reduce unwanted technical variation preserving biologically meaningful spatial expression patterns within across tissue slices. uses pre-identified biological regions, referred niches, encourage consistency average biological signals across matched regions different tissue slices.

title: Spatially Aware Normalisation for Multi-Slice Spatial Transcriptomics Data
text: development version MultiNorm can installed directly GitHub: Load package:
code: # Install remotes if required install.packages("remotes")  # Install MultiNorm remotes::install_github("Lahiru-lsb/MultiNorm") library(MultiNorm)

title: Spatially Aware Normalisation for Multi-Slice Spatial Transcriptomics Data
text: MultiNorm accepts named list SpatialExperiment objects, object represents individual tissue slice. object contain: raw gene expression count matrix. Two-dimensional spatial coordinates. Spot-level biological niche annotations. common set genes across tissue slices. Niche annotations represent biologically comparable regions across slices. annotations can obtained using spatial clustering integration methods, existing biological annotations.

title: Spatially Aware Normalisation for Multi-Slice Spatial Transcriptomics Data
text: default, MultiNorm returns list normalised SpatialExperiment objects. example user-specified parameters shown :
code: library(MultiNorm)  # Normalise multiple tissue slices norm_spe <- MultiNorm(   spe_list = spe_list,   niche_col = "niche" ) # Access the first normalised tissue slice norm_slice1 <- norm_spe[[1]]  # Access normalised gene expression SummarizedExperiment::logcounts(norm_slice1) norm_spe <- MultiNorm(   spe_list = spe_list,   niche_col = "niche",   spot_frac = 0.5,   df_bio = c(6, 6),   df_tech = c(3, 3),   lambdaC = 10000,   lambda1 = 0.01,   lambda2 = 2,   seed = 123,   verbose = TRUE )

title: Spatially Aware Normalisation for Multi-Slice Spatial Transcriptomics Data
text: Fitted model parameters can returned together normalised data setting return_fit = TRUE.
code: result <- MultiNorm(   spe_list = spe_list,   niche_col = "niche",   return_fit = TRUE )  norm_spe <- result$norm_spe fit <- result$fit

title: Spatially Aware Normalisation for Multi-Slice Spatial Transcriptomics Data

Performing basic quality control. Selecting common highly variable genes. Identifying biologically similar niches across slices. Applying MultiNorm. Comparing library size distributions normalisation. access installed vignette:

title: Normalize multislice spatial transcriptomics (ST) data — MultiNorm
text: Performs normalization multislice ST data using negative binomial model spatial biological effects, library-size-associated technical effects, slice-specific technical intercept deviations.

title: Normalize multislice spatial transcriptomics (ST) data — MultiNorm
code: MultiNorm(   spe_list,   niche_col,   preferred_niches = NULL,   spot_frac = 1,   verbose = FALSE,   df_bio = c(6, 6),   df_tech = c(3, 3),   lambdaC = 10000,   lambda1 = 0.01,   lambda2 = 2,   max_outer = 20,   max_inner = 100,   tol_disp = 1e-04,   tol_param = 1e-05,   psi_damp = 1,   param_damp = 0.2,   seed = 1,   alpha_init = NULL,   Beta_init = NULL,   Gamma_init = NULL,   Psi_init = NULL,   zeta_init = NULL,   rho_init = NULL,   A = NULL,   return_fit = FALSE )

title: Normalize multislice spatial transcriptomics (ST) data — MultiNorm
text: spe_list List SpatialExperiment objects, one per slice. object must contain column spot-level niche annotations. niche_col Character integer. Column name index colData specifying niche labels. Niches represent biologically similar clusters shared across slices. preferred_niches Optional vector specifying subset niche labels. Default NULL, case shared niches used. spot_frac Numeric (0, 1]. Proportion spots sample model fitting. Default 1. verbose Logical. TRUE, prints sampling details. Default FALSE. df_bio Numeric vector length 2 specifying degrees freedom two-dimensional spline basis used model biological spatial effects. Default c(6, 6). df_tech Numeric vector length 2 specifying degrees freedom two-dimensional spline basis used model library-size-associated technical effects. Default c(3, 3). lambdaC Numeric. Penalty coefficient enforcing similarity biological effects across matched niches slices. Default 10000. lambda1 Numeric. Ridge regularization parameter biological spline coefficients. Default 0.01. lambda2 Numeric. Ridge regularization parameter technical spline coefficients. Default 2. max_outer Integer. Maximum number outer iterations dispersion updates. Default 20. max_inner Integer. Maximum number inner IRWLS iterations model parameter updates. Default 100. tol_disp Numeric. Convergence tolerance dispersion updates. Default 1e-4. tol_param Numeric. Convergence tolerance inner-loop parameter updates. Default 1e-5. psi_damp Numeric (0, 1]. Damping factor dispersion updates. Default 1. param_damp Numeric (0, 1]. Damping factor IRWLS parameter updates. Default 0.2. seed Integer. Random seed used spot subsampling. Default 1. alpha_init Optional numeric vector initial values slice-specific global library-size effects. length equal number slices. Default NULL. Beta_init Optional list initial biological spline coefficient matrices. element dimension Kb x G, Kb number biological spline basis functions G number genes. Default NULL. Gamma_init Optional list initial technical spline coefficient matrices. element dimension Kt x G, Kt number technical spline basis functions. Default NULL. Psi_init Optional list initial dispersion vectors. element length G. Default NULL. zeta_init Optional numeric vector initial values global gene-specific intercepts. length G. Default NULL. rho_init Optional matrix initial values slice-deviation contrast parameters. dimension (S - 1) x G, S number slices G number genes. Default NULL. Optional sum--zero contrast matrix slice-specific technical deviations. dimension S x (S - 1) satisfy colSums() == 0. NULL, default contrast matrix constructed internally. return_fit Logical. TRUE, returns fitted model parameters along normalized data. Default FALSE.

title: Normalize multislice spatial transcriptomics (ST) data — MultiNorm
text: return_fit = FALSE, returns list   SpatialExperiment objects normalized values stored   norm_spe. return_fit = TRUE, returns list containing: norm_spe: normalized SpatialExperiment objects. fit: fitted model parameters. call: matched function call. Eta_full_list: fitted full linear predictors slice. percentiles: fitted NB percentiles used PAC transformation.

title: Normalize multislice spatial transcriptomics (ST) data — MultiNorm
text: method fits negative binomial model spatial biological effects, library-size-associated technical effects, slice-specific technical intercept deviations. Biological technical effects modeled using two-dimensional spline bases. Cross-slice biological consistency encouraged matched niche-level constraints applied biological spline component. model includes global gene-specific intercept slice-specific technical intercept deviation represented using sum--zero contrasts. allows slice-level technical shifts explained library size modeled explicitly, preserving biological niche-matching constraint biological component. Parameter estimation performed using iteratively reweighted least squares (IRWLS), outer-loop updates negative binomial dispersion parameters.
